name: Yusuf Farah

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a senior researcher with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal workday like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43, have an MBA and lead nine complaint specialists inside a large company. After twelve years with the team I can usually settle the case nobody else wants, and I train leads on when to give an agent authority to fix a delivery. I hate seeing a customer get a fourth polite script. I have never used an AI tool; the case record and a phone call are what I trust.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How is your household doing alongside the work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner drives delivery shifts that change week to week, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. My pay is low for this manager job after a long band freeze, we have barely three weeks of expenses saved, and there are few comparable roles nearby. I know I am good at this work; I still count the heating bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my escalation team that a small automated reply might help with opening hours, but a customer whose service failed twice deserves a person who can put it right. I don't want our best staff chasing a faster greeting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I lead nine complaint specialists and have an MBA, but the company pays this team below comparable managers and has frozen the band for years. My partner's delivery driving shifts vary, we have two children at school and a mortgage, and our savings cover barely three weeks; a plateau leaves that pressure where it is.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: On Monday I'll keep the daily case review and ask my senior specialist to flag any automatic reply that repeats the customer's complaint without solving it. In the first year of the plateau, I'll take three resolved cases to HR for a pay-band review and stop the paid sports channel, 25 a month, putting that money into cash after the mortgage if it is still free.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the mortgage, not the little AI reply. One slow delivery week can make a good workday feel useless by dinner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does a resolved case look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A customer's replacement part was sent to the wrong depot twice, and the third agent finally called the warehouse instead of sending another script. I gave that agent authority to arrange delivery; the customer called back to say it had arrived.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why stay on this pay band?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My team knows me and there are very few comparable manager posts nearby. I would consider a genuine offer, but I won't leave a known wage on the strength of a vacancy advert.

say: I'd keep a **person with authority** on repeated service failures.
I'd tell staff a **faster greeting** cannot replace a fixed delivery.
think: My **low manager pay** and a frozen band leave the mortgage exposed despite strong work.
Variable driving shifts and **three-week savings** make a plateau financially tight.
do: Keep **daily case reviews** and flag replies that repeat problems without solving them.
Take **three resolved cases** to HR for a pay-band review; cancel sports television and save 25 after mortgage if available.
feel: He feels **anxious** about the mortgage despite little AI change.
S0.quote: One slow delivery week can make a good workday feel useless by dinner.
fieldNote: His **high skill** has not translated into pay or cash, and few nearby roles limit easy exits.
His case story shows **authority to fix delivery**, not only skill at saying sorry.

steps.text: Keep daily escalation case reviews with nine specialists
Cancel paid sports channel to free 25 monthly
Save freed 25 monthly after mortgage if available

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the contact centre Steady Disruption will write replies, route calls and plan shifts, and workers should see the proposed staffing levels before a dashboard replaces those tasks. I would ask our union representative for an agreement on who can overturn a wrong automated answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can settle difficult complaints quickly, but a company could keep one expert and cut several team leads, including me. My partner's variable driving pay won't replace my wage, and there are few similar jobs within a school-day drive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll collect the cases where an automated reply made a complaint worse and take them to the union representative with the proposed staffing chart request. In the first year of disruption, if the company merges team leads, I'd apply for a senior customer resolution vacancy at the regional service office only after checking posted pay and hours against the mortgage and school pickup; I would keep my current job until a written offer arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a smaller leadership team, and angry when speed is counted as care. I know how to change a bad call, but I don't know how to make directors price that work fairly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you learn the new AI reply tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used AI myself and don't plan to become its tester. I'd read the error log and let trained colleagues show me what the tool gets wrong, while I keep the appeal route open.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the union need to see?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The number of leads removed, who signs a reversed decision, and whether workers have time to appeal a bad score. I want those terms in writing before the first monthly target is set.

say: I'd ask for **staffing levels** before automated replies and routing change the contact centre.
I'd seek a **union agreement** on overturning wrong answers and scores.
think: My strong casework may not prevent **team lead cuts**, including my own role.
Variable partner pay and scarce local jobs leave the **mortgage exposed** if my wage stops.
do: Bring **failed automated replies** and staffing questions to the union representative this week.
If leads merge, check **regional resolution vacancy** pay and pickup hours before applying; stay until written offer.
feel: He feels **anxious and angry** about losing a role whose careful work may be scored as slow.
S1.quote: I know how to change a bad call, but I don't know how to make directors price that work fairly.
fieldNote: His private fear is **manager consolidation**, while his public demand centers workers' appeal rights.
He remains **resistant to AI use**, reading colleagues' tests instead of claiming a new tool skill.

steps.text: Bring failed automated replies and staffing questions to union representative
Apply regionally after lead merger if pay and pickup fit; stay until written offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my team AGI by 2028 can handle almost every routine complaint and much of the hard reasoning too, so staff need notice before any posts disappear. I'd demand a named person who can reverse an automated refusal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My desk and judgment face AGI in 2028; robots around 2031 might handle physical deliveries later, but they do not protect the complaint role. I expect my lead post could go, and three weeks of cash means the mortgage would be at risk before I found a comparable job nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I'll ask the union for written severance and appeal terms, then put the mortgage due date and our last three payslips on the kitchen table with my partner. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, if I lose the role, I'd apply for a local service manager opening only if posted pay covers the mortgage and childcare, accept only a written offer, and check eligibility for any job-loss support before counting it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I can picture the mortgage letter arriving before the next wage. My skills are real, but the bank won't take a successful complaint as payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell them we may pause the paid weekend swimming class, 60 a month, only if my salary stops; I would not call it a punishment. My partner and I would ask the school whether a free pool session exists before removing swimming altogether.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would customer resolution at another firm survive AGI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No; a different logo doesn't change the thinking work. I would take a real wage if offered, but I'd keep looking at roles that include accountable decisions rather than promise the children a safe title.

say: I'd demand **notice and reversals** before automated complaint decisions remove posts.
I'd tell staff **complaint reasoning** changes in 2028, before delivery robots arrive.
think: My **skilled desk work** faces 2028 AGI; 2031 robots offer no delay.
Three weeks saved and few local posts put the **mortgage at risk** after a lost wage.
do: Request **severance and appeal terms** through the union and review mortgage dates now.
After 2028, seek **local service work** only with posted mortgage-and-care pay; accept only a written offer.
feel: He feels **alarmed** by how soon a lost wage could reach the mortgage.
S2.quote: My skills are real, but the bank won't take a successful complaint as payment.
fieldNote: His **senior skill** does not shield thinking work from the 2028 system or refill a three-week reserve.
A local service role is **also exposed**; the swimming cut and support claim remain conditional.

steps.text: Ask union for written severance and complaint appeal terms now
Apply locally after cut only if posted pay covers mortgage and childcare; accept written offer
Pause 60 monthly swimming class only if his salary stops

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AGI by 2031 gives us five years to put a proper appeal rule into every complaint process and to plan for roles with real authority. I would ask the union to negotiate those rules before the software is bought.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years might let us put two months of expenses aside if my partner's driving shifts become regular. Yet even the difficult cases and appeal decisions are thinking work AGI may do in 2031; robots around 2034 are a later risk for physical deliveries, not a delay for me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting next winter, if the union runs its free conflict-resolution workshop after my partner can cover the children's evening pickup, I'd take it and practise leading a real appeal meeting. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, I'd seek an internal appeals manager vacancy only if it exists at pay covering the mortgage; otherwise I'd look at nearby employers while keeping my present wage until a written offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about learning a new part of a job that might itself shrink. Five years is time to improve, but not an assurance that the company will keep a person on appeals.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you make the two-month cushion?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if driving shifts are booked regularly would we put an extra 80 monthly into cash after the mortgage. I won't write that 80 into the family plan while the app still changes my partner's work every week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why learn appeals if AGI could do them?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Because someone must insist a person can contest a wrong decision now, not just after 2031. I am learning how to hear a worker's appeal, not buying a guarantee of a job.

say: I'd seek **union-negotiated appeals** before the company buys the system.
I'd ask for **real authority** in any post that remains after 2031.
think: A **two-month reserve** might be possible if driving shifts become regular.
Hard cases and appeals are **thinking work** exposed in 2031; later robots do not delay my desk.
do: Take a **free conflict workshop** next winter only if union offers it and evening pickup is covered.
Save **80 monthly** after mortgage only when driving shifts are regularly booked; seek real appeals vacancy after 2031.
If none exists, check **nearby jobs** while retaining current wage until a written offer.
feel: He feels **uneasy** about studying exposed work and anxious about the current cash margin.
S3.quote: I am learning how to hear a worker's appeal, not buying a guarantee of a job.
fieldNote: He sees **appeals as exposed**, yet values a contestable decision now, independent of career safety.
The workshop and savings are gated by **family time** and booked shifts, matching his thin cushion.

steps.text: Take free union conflict workshop if offered and partner covers evening pickup
Save extra 80 monthly after mortgage only when driving shifts are regularly booked
Apply for internal appeals manager after 2031 only if vacancy pays mortgage
Apply nearby if no appeals post exists, keeping current wage until written offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the union AGI by 2036 gives a decade to require human appeals and paid retraining before staff are moved. I would ask for yearly figures on who actually keeps a wage after a role changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll be 53 when thinking AI arrives, and our children will be older, but the mortgage may still be there. My experience could help me lead a fair complaint process for years; AGI may still perform that reasoning in 2036, and robots around 2039 add no time to this desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep leading the nine specialists and ask the union to review our appeal cases every quarter. I'd also negotiate a pay-band review again, using the three resolved cases, and put any actual increase into emergency cash after the mortgage; in the first year after 2036, I'd stay only for a paid role with authority to reverse bad decisions, otherwise apply to nearby posts while keeping my wage until a written offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel watchful, but not relieved by ten years. A decade helps with planning, while this week's delivery shifts still decide whether we can save anything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for better pay before 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after my partner and I priced the children's schools and the mortgage, and only for an actual offer. There are few local management posts, but moving on a rumor could cost us more than a raise would bring.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a fair process mean to you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The person taking the complaint must be able to change the decision, not only explain it. A title that cannot reverse a bad answer is a nameplate on a locked door.

say: I'd seek **human appeals** and paid retraining through the union before 2036.
I'd demand **yearly wage outcomes** for staff whose roles change.
think: At **53**, the children will be older but the mortgage may remain.
Experience does not exempt **complaint reasoning** from 2036 AGI; 2039 robots add no desk delay.
do: Keep **nine specialists** working and bring quarterly appeals to the union this year.
Request a **pay-band review** with three cases; save any real increase after mortgage.
After 2036, stay for **paid reversal authority**; otherwise apply nearby while keeping wage until a written offer.
feel: He feels **watchful**, with ten years to plan but a thin cash margin today.
S4.quote: A title that cannot reverse a bad answer is a nameplate on a locked door.
fieldNote: His long-run move is a **pay claim** and union rule, not a vague switch to new technology.
The **three-week cushion** keeps present household uncertainty alive despite a decade of lead time.

steps.text: Keep leading nine complaint specialists this year
Bring quarterly appeal cases to union review
Save any actual pay-band increase after mortgage payment
Apply nearby after 2036 if no paid reversal authority, keeping wage until written offer

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because even our hard complaints could be handled cheaply before our family has cash to cover a lost wage. Written staffing and severance terms, a real appeal authority and a viable paid opening would help me protect the mortgage.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who can fix the failed delivery after a machine sends its fourth apology. A customer needs a person allowed to change the order, not another sentence.

headlineQuote: A customer needs a person allowed to change the order, not another sentence.
portrait: At **43**, Yusuf is an MBA-trained senior complaint manager with deep case skill and no personal AI use.
His **low pay**, variable partner shifts, mortgage and three-week reserve keep him anxious even in a plateau.
He asks the **union for written terms** and insists appeals have real reversal power.
Fast AGI threatens **complaint reasoning**; longer runways offer preparation, though appeals remain thinking-exposed.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his strong but underpaid role before he can protect the mortgage.
whatWouldHelp: **Written staffing terms**, real reversal authority and a viable paid opening would help his family plan.
